subject: KMS bridge proposal: HSM-proxy patterns and network controls
messages:
From: Liam O'Connell <liam.oconnell@edgewave.io>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: security@edgewave.io
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2027 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: KMS bridge: HSM-proxy pattern proposal + network constraints

Jonas,

Thanks for taking this. We're preparing our private deployment (EdgeWave VPC) onboarding checklist and need to nail down the key custody model. High level constraints from our end:

- Master keys must remain in our on-prem HSM (FIPS 140-2 Level 3) — no plaintext KEKs leaving our boundary.
- We need strong audit trails (per-wrap/unwrap events, operator identity), with logs retained for 1 year.
- Network egress is tightly limited; any proxy/connector must originate from our VPC and use mutual TLS to the HSM gateway.
- We prefer an on-call operator flow for initial key import (manual ceremony) and an automated rewrap path for rotations.

Attached is a short requirements doc (edgewave-kms-requirements.pdf). Can Redwood outline a pattern that avoids storing customer KEKs in Redwood while allowing the Redwood inference runtime to get DEKs for encryption of persisted artifacts and cache snapshots?

Also: what are the failure/fallback modes if the HSM is temporarily unreachable? We need to ensure no silent fallback to Redwood-managed keys unless explicitly agreed and documented.

Cheers,
Liam O'Connell
Security Engineer, EdgeWave
liam.oconnell@edgewave.io

Attachment: edgewave-kms-requirements.pdf (PDF, 360KB)

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Liam O'Connell <liam.oconnell@edgewave.io>
Cc: Rebecca Marsh <rebecca.marsh@edgewave.io>, Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2027 11:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: KMS bridge: HSM-proxy pattern proposal + network constraints

Liam — thanks for the clear constraints and the doc. We're aligned on the core goals: customer KEKs never in plaintext in Redwood, per-event audit, and explicit agreement for any fallback. Below is a proposed pattern for discussion. I'll schedule a short design review once you confirm this direction.

Proposed pattern (summary):
- Envelope encryption: Redwood runtime generates ephemeral DEKs for data at rest and caches. DEKs are encrypted (wrapped) using your KEK inside your HSM. Redwood stores only the wrapped DEKs.
- HSM bridge/proxy: a lightweight connector (customer-controlled) runs in your VPC and exposes a strictly-scoped RPC to perform WrapKey / UnwrapKey operations. Connector authenticates to HSM via PKCS#11 (or HSM vendor agent) and to Redwood via mutual TLS with a client cert we provide.
- Network: Only outbound connections from Redwood to the connector allowed, via an approved IP + port list. The connector allows connections only from Redwood's service certificate. TLS with mTLS + certificate pinning required.
- Audit: Connector logs wrap/unwrap events to your SIEM and mirrors a signed event to Redwood (signed token with nonce) so both parties have tamper-evident records.
- Rotation: KEK rotation is initiated by your security team. On rotation, the connector exposes a bulk rewrap job (reauth'd and operator-approved). Redwood will re-encrypt persisted wrapped-DEKs using the new wrapped-KEK only after operator approval.
- Fallback: We do not perform automatic fallback to Redwood-managed KEKs. If the HSM is unreachable we offer a clearly-labelled 'degraded mode' that requires a documented operator exception and will be gated by an ACL + signed approval (DocuSign link if you want).

To move forward we need:
1) A network diagram for the connector placement (in-scope subnets/NAT/etc).
2) Connector deployment model: container/VM image; we can provide an image that you run in your VPC or you can build one from our published config.
3) Audit schema: sample signed event format (we'll send a draft).

I'll propose times for a 45-minute review. cc'ing Tessa and Priyom to start a checklist and confirm the connector build options.

— Jonas
Jonas Weber
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.ai

Attachment: none

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2027 13:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: KMS bridge: HSM-proxy pattern proposal + network controls (internal)

Internal notes / changes to the pattern:
- Use PKCS#11 for supported HSMs (YubiHSM, Thales Luna, nCipher) and vendor agent for others. We should include a fallback connector that supports KMIP for legacy HSMs.
- Connector image: we'll publish a hardened container (distroless) that performs only Wrap/Unwrap and health-check endpoints (no admin API). Customer runs it in a private subnet with egress to Redwood's endpoint via NAT.
- Health & circuit breaker: add a token-based rate limit + a signed health heartbeat. If health fails for > config threshold, flag for operator approval; do not auto-unlock any DEKs.
- Rotation orchestration: Priyom to own an orchestration script (idempotent) that can perform bulk rewraps via the connector using an operator-signed schedule. We'll also record a per-key rewrap manifest.

Action owners:
- Priyom: draft connector manifest + rewrap orchestration (ETA: 2027-09-21)
- Hiro: design audit event schema and signed token format (ETA: 2027-09-20)
- Jonas: draft network diagram and meeting invite (in flight)

Tessa
Director, Product Security

From: Rebecca Marsh <rebecca.marsh@edgewave.io>

Subject: Re: KMS bridge: HSM-proxy pattern proposal + network controls

Thanks — this looks promising. A few follow-ups from EdgeWave security: 

1) Key import: we will do an initial manual import/ceremony for the KEK via PKCS#11 (operator present). For subsequent rotations we'd like an automated import path where we can push new KEK public material via a signed CSR flow and operator acceptance. Can your connector support both manual and CSR-based imports?

2) Audit retention: we'd like Redwood to retain a copy of signed wrap/unwrap event summaries for 90 days (full detail stays in our SIEM). Are you comfortable with that?

3) Network & egress: we will run the connector in a private subnet with an explicit route to Redwood's IP range. No internet egress allowed except to Redwood's pinned IPs.

4) DocuSign: we need an operator access exception form for a potential degraded-mode unlock. Please send a draft.

We can take the architecture diagram and the manifest once you produce them. Also — can you include an example audit token we can validate against our HSM signing keys?

Best,
Rebecca Marsh
Head of Security Operations, EdgeWave
rebecca.marsh@edgewave.io

- Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/spaces/ENG/pages/KB-12345-kms-bridge-design
- Draft DocuSign operator exception: https://docusign.com/Envelope/0A1B2C3D4E

Short design notes:
- Connector responsibilities: Wrap/Unwrap, health, per-op signed receipts. No persistence beyond transient logs destined for customer's SIEM.
- Connector deployment options: (A) customer-run image (recommended), (B) customer-build from published manifest. We'll provide hardened container and a minimal Helm chart.
- Auth: Redwood will provide an mTLS client cert; connector will accept only pinned certs. Additional signing of audit receipts will use an HSM key and a signed JWT with nonce.
- Offline ceremony: We'll include a runbook for manual import (PKCS#11 key generation + verification) — operator-to-operator checklist included in the mutual-action-plan spreadsheet.

Next steps: confirm a meeting time and Priyom/Hiro will circulate the draft schemas prior to the call.

— Jonas
